methods.name: Apply
methods.description:
Create or update an agent runner.

 @internal
 Primary registration path for CLI/Desktop runners. The handler determines
 whether to create or update based on whether the resource already exists
 (resolved by org + slug). Authorization is handled in the handler.

methods.name: Create
methods.description:
Create a new agent runner.

 @internal
 Authorization: Caller must have can_create_agent_runner permission in the
 organization. The server generates the task queue name (agent-runner:{id})
 and sets the initial phase to PENDING.

methods.name: Update
methods.description:
Update an existing agent runner.

 @internal
 Used for updating spec fields (e.g., description). Status fields are
 updated via heartbeat, not via this RPC.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description:
Delete an agent runner.

 @internal
 For persistent runners: removes the resource and its task queue.
 For system-managed runners: called by the execution workflow during
 cleanup after the execution completes.

methods.name: Heartbeat
methods.description:
Report runner liveness and operational state.

 Called by the runner process every 30 seconds. Updates status fields
 (phase, last_heartbeat_at, current_executions, connection_info) without
 modifying spec or metadata.

 If the runner is in PENDING or STOPPED phase, a heartbeat transitions it
 to the phase reported in the input (typically READY). This enables the
 "restart and reconnect" flow: a stopped runner resumes heartbeating and
 goes back to READY with the same identity and task queue.

 @internal
 Authorization is handled in the handler: the caller must own the runner.
 Skipped at the interceptor level because the input is AgentRunnerHeartbeatInput
 (not a resource), and the ownership check requires a DB lookup.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get a single agent runner by ID.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description:
Get an agent runner by its organization-scoped reference (org/slug).

 Used by the CLI to resolve a runner by name:
   stigmer run agent my-agent --runner my-macbook
 resolves "my-macbook" to the full AgentRunner resource.

 @internal
 Custom authorization in handler — checks both direct resource access
 and organization-level visibility permissions.

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List agent runners within an organization.

 Supports label-based filtering for common use cases:
 - Session composer: exclude system-managed runners, show only READY/IDLE
 - Admin view: show all runners including system-managed
 - Debugging: filter by specific labels

 @internal
 Authorization is handled in-handler via FGA-filtered queries (cloud)
 or unrestricted store queries (OSS).

methodTypes.name: AgentRunnerHeartbeatInput
methodTypes.description:
AgentRunnerHeartbeatInput is sent by the runner process on a regular
 interval (default 30s) to report liveness and operational state.

 The server uses heartbeat absence to detect stale runners: if no heartbeat
 arrives within the timeout window (default 90s = 3x interval), the runner
 transitions to STOPPED. When a stopped runner resumes heartbeating, it
 transitions back to READY.

 The heartbeat is intentionally lightweight — it carries only the fields that
 change frequently. Static runner identity (name, org, description) is set
 once via create/apply and does not repeat on every heartbeat.

fields.name: AgentRunnerId
fields.description: ID of the agent runner sending the heartbeat.

fields.name: Phase
fields.description:
Current operational phase as reported by the runner.
 Typically READY (accepting work) or BUSY (at capacity).

fields.name: CurrentExecutions
fields.description: Number of agent executions currently in progress on this runner.

fields.name: ConnectionInfo
fields.description:
Self-reported machine information. The runner sends this on every
 heartbeat so that version upgrades and hostname changes are reflected
 without requiring a full resource update.

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource by org and slug.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Environment, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical format: "org/slug" (e.g., "stigmer/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource.

 When non-empty: must be a valid org slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 1-63 characters). Example: "stigmer", "acme-corp".

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 Use explicit org for cross-org references (e.g., marketplace resources).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, MCP_SERVER).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 1-63 characters.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

enumTypes.name: AgentRunnerPhase
enumTypes.description:
AgentRunnerPhase tracks the operational state of an agent runner process.

 Phase transitions are driven by two sources:
 - The runner process itself (via heartbeat RPC): PENDING -> READY, READY <-> BUSY
 - The server (via heartbeat timeout or explicit stop): any -> STOPPED, any -> FAILED

 Transition diagram:
   PENDING  -> READY   (first heartbeat received)
   READY    -> BUSY    (runner reports max capacity reached)
   BUSY     -> READY   (runner reports capacity freed)
   READY    -> STOPPED (heartbeat timeout or explicit stop)
   BUSY     -> STOPPED (heartbeat timeout or explicit stop)
   STOPPED  -> READY   (runner restarts and heartbeats again)
   any      -> FAILED  (unrecoverable error reported by runner or server)

values.name: AGENT_RUNNER_PHASE_PENDING
values.description:
Resource created but no heartbeat received yet.
 This is the initial phase after create/apply, before the runner
 process has started polling its task queue and heartbeating.

values.name: AGENT_RUNNER_PHASE_READY
values.description: Runner is heartbeating and accepting new executions.

values.name: AGENT_RUNNER_PHASE_BUSY
values.description:
Runner is heartbeating but at maximum concurrent execution capacity.
 New executions should not be dispatched to this runner.

values.name: AGENT_RUNNER_PHASE_STOPPED
values.description:
Runner has stopped heartbeating (timeout) or was explicitly stopped.
 The resource is retained for identity persistence — a runner that
 restarts and resumes heartbeating transitions back to READY.

values.name: AGENT_RUNNER_PHASE_FAILED
values.description:
Unrecoverable error. Runner or server reported a fatal condition.
 Requires investigation; does not auto-recover on heartbeat.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines whether
 users outside that organization can access the resource.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only members of the owning organization can access.
 This is the default for most resources.
 Named visibility_private to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Anyone can access (read) this resource.
 Used for marketplace-published resources (e.g., "stigmer/web-search").
 Write access still requires org membership.
 Named visibility_public to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

resourceDescription:
AgentRunner represents a process that executes agent work.

 Runners are the computational backbone of the Stigmer platform. Every agent
 execution runs on a runner — whether auto-created by the platform for a cloud
 execution or started by a user on their own machine via CLI or desktop app.

 AgentRunner follows the Kubernetes Node pattern:
 - **Thin spec**: the user declares intent (a name, a description). That's it.
 - **Rich status**: the runner process self-reports everything via heartbeat —
   phase, capacity, machine info, task queue.
 - **Identity persists across restarts**: a runner that stops and restarts
   reconnects to the same resource. The CLI stores the runner ID locally and
   calls apply to reactivate the same identity, same queue.

 Two creation patterns:
 - **User-created (persistent)**: user runs `stigmer runner start`, runner
   appears in the session composer, user selects it for their sessions.
 - **System-managed (ephemeral)**: platform auto-creates a runner for a cloud
   execution, labels it stigmer.ai/system-managed: "true", tears it down when
   the execution completes. Hidden from the session composer.

 Sessions bind to a runner via SessionSpec.agent_runner_id. Executions record
 which runner handled them via AgentExecutionStatus.agent_runner_id.

statusType.name: AgentRunnerStatus
statusType.description:
AgentRunnerStatus contains all operational state for a runner.

 Every field here is either system-managed (phase, task_queue, sandbox_id) or
 runner-reported via heartbeat (last_heartbeat_at, current_executions,
 connection_info). None of it is user-declared — that separation is the
 spec/status invariant.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, created_by, etc.)

fields.name: Phase
fields.description: Current operational phase of the runner process.

fields.name: TaskQueue
fields.description:
Temporal task queue this runner polls for work.
 Format: "agent-runner:{runner-id}"
 Set by the server when the runner resource is created; immutable after.
 The execution workflow reads this field to route activities to the runner.

fields.name: LastHeartbeatAt
fields.description:
Timestamp of the last successful heartbeat from the runner process.
 Used by the server to detect stale runners: if now - last_heartbeat_at
 exceeds the heartbeat timeout (default 90s), the phase transitions to
 STOPPED.

fields.name: StartedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when this runner first transitioned to READY.

fields.name: StoppedAt
fields.description:
Timestamp when this runner last transitioned to STOPPED or FAILED.
 Empty while the runner is active (PENDING, READY, or BUSY).

fields.name: CurrentExecutions
fields.description:
Number of agent executions currently in progress on this runner.
 Reported by the runner on each heartbeat. Used by the dispatch logic
 to determine runner availability and load.

fields.name: SandboxId
fields.description:
Sandbox ID for cloud runners that execute inside a Daytona sandbox.
 Empty for local runners (CLI, Docker) that use the host filesystem.
 Set by the platform when the sandbox is created; immutable after.

fields.name: ConnectionInfo
fields.description:
Self-reported information about the machine running this runner.
 Populated by the runner process on each heartbeat.

statusNestedTypes.name: AgentRunnerConnectionInfo
statusNestedTypes.description:
AgentRunnerConnectionInfo contains self-reported details about the runner's
 host environment. Populated by the runner process on each heartbeat call.

 This information is used for:
 - UI display: "Alice's MacBook Pro (darwin/arm64)"
 - Debugging: matching runner behavior to specific OS/arch combinations
 - Version tracking: ensuring runners stay up-to-date

fields.name: Hostname
fields.description:
Hostname or user-friendly machine name.
 Example: "Alice's MacBook Pro", "ci-runner-3.internal"

fields.name: Os
fields.description:
Operating system reported by the runner process.
 Example: "darwin", "linux", "windows"

fields.name: Arch
fields.description:
CPU architecture reported by the runner process.
 Example: "arm64", "amd64"

fields.name: RunnerVersion
fields.description:
Version of the agent-runner software.
 Example: "0.4.2"
